us: Me and at least one other person, excluding the person(s) being addressed.
usability: The state or condition of being usable.
usance: The length of time permitted for the payment of a bill of exchange.
used: simple past and past participle of use
useful: Having a practical or beneficial use.
usefully: In a useful manner; in a way that achieves something
usefulness: The quality or degree of being useful.
useless: Without use or the possibility to be used.
uselessness: The state or quality of being useless.
user: One who uses or makes use of something, a consumer or client or an express or implied licensee (free user) or a trespasser.
usher: A person, in a church, cinema etc., who escorts people to their seats.
ushered: simple past and past participle of usher
ushering: present participle and gerund of usher
using: present participle and gerund of use
usnea: Any lichen of the genus Usnea.
usually: Most of the time; less than always, but more than occasionally.
usualness: The quality or state of being usual.
usufruct: The legal right to use and derive profit or benefit from property that belongs to another person, as long as the property is not damaged.
usufructuary: Of or pertaining to a usufruct.
usurer: A person who loans money to others and charges interest, particularly at an exorbitant, exploitative, or illegal rate.
usurp: To seize and hold or use (powers, an office, a coat of arms, a right or copyright, etc) from another, without right (usually by illegitimate means).
usurpation: The wrongful seizure of something by force, especially of sovereignty or other authority.
usurped: simple past and past participle of usurp
usurping: present participle and gerund of usurp
usurps: third-person singular simple present indicative of usurp
usury: An exorbitant rate of interest, in excess of any legal rates or at least immorally.
